description:
## Symptom
Next.js 16.2.4 boot prints:
```
⚠ The "middleware" file convention is deprecated. Please use "proxy" instead.
Learn more: https://nextjs.org/docs/messages/middleware-to-proxy
```

Currently a warning, not an error. Will become a hard error in a future Next major.

## Background
The `middleware.ts` file convention is being renamed to `proxy.ts`. Both work in Next 16; only `proxy.ts` will work in the next major bump.

After the d3700325 refactor, our middleware is minimal — just the `clerkMiddleware` wrapper passing through to handlers, plus the matcher config. The rename is therefore mechanical: same default export, same matcher.

## Migration steps
1. `git mv src/middleware.ts src/proxy.ts`
2. Confirm the default export shape is unchanged (clerkMiddleware wrapper from @clerk/nextjs/server still applies — Clerk supports the proxy convention in their Next 16 compatibility track).
3. Update file-level docstring: `src/middleware.ts` → `src/proxy.ts`.
4. Check the migration doc (https://nextjs.org/docs/messages/middleware-to-proxy) for any matcher-config syntax changes; update if needed.
5. Update `src/__tests__/admin.test.ts` import path (`@/middleware` → `@/proxy`).
6. `npx vitest run` — all admin-* tests should pass unchanged.
7. `npm run dev` — confirm the deprecation warning is gone.

## Acceptance
- No deprecation warning at boot.
- All admin-* tests pass.
- Production deploys identically (the file convention rename is a Next-runtime concern, not a build-output concern).

## Related
- Surfaced post-d3700325 (PR #57) when the user ran dev locally.
- Likely candidate to bundle with other Next 16 deprecation cleanups when they accumulate. Currently this is the only one we've hit.
